scenes.tts: Take a patient's skin cells, reset them, and grow them for weeks in a spinning flask. Can that model their early cortex?
scenes.visual: Title card: The Program and the Surroundings. A skin cell, a spinning flask, and a small ball of tissue, joined by arrows ending in a question mark.
scenes.narration: Take a patient's skin cells, reset them, and grow them for weeks in a spinning flask. Can that model their early cortex?

scenes.tts: First, the skin cell must go back to an embryonic state. Four transcription factors can do that.
scenes.visual: A flat skin cell; four labelled factor shapes (Oct3/4, Sox2, Klf4, c-Myc) drift toward its nucleus.
scenes.narration: First, the skin cell must go back to an embryonic state. Four transcription factors can do that.

scenes.tts: Transcription factors are proteins that bind DNA and switch genes on or off.
scenes.visual: The four factors attach to a strand of DNA; gene segments light up or dim as they bind.
scenes.narration: Transcription factors are proteins that bind DNA and switch genes on or off.

scenes.tts: The result is an induced pluripotent stem cell, an i P S cell. Pluripotent means it can become any cell type of the body.
scenes.caption: The result is an induced pluripotent stem cell, an iPS cell. Pluripotent means it can become any cell type of the body.
scenes.visual: The skin cell rounds up into a stem cell, labelled iPS cell. Small icons of many cell types fan out from it, labelled pluripotent.
scenes.narration: The result is an induced pluripotent stem cell, an iPS cell. Pluripotent means it can become any cell type of the body.

scenes.tts: A line made from a patient carries the patient's genome, mutation included. It can also pick up new changes in culture.
scenes.visual: A chromosome set inside the stem cell, with one gene marked in red as the mutation and a few small grey marks labelled new changes in culture.
scenes.narration: A line made from a patient carries the patient's genome, mutation included. It can also pick up new changes in culture.

scenes.tts: The recipe has four steps. First, gather the stem cells into a ball.
scenes.visual: Step card 1 of 4, Aggregate: stem cells cluster into a ball, labelled embryoid body.
scenes.narration: The recipe has four steps. First, gather the stem cells into a ball.

scenes.tts: Steer it toward neural tissue.
scenes.visual: Step card 2 of 4, Steer: the ball's outer cells turn teal, labelled neural tissue.
scenes.narration: Steer it toward neural tissue.

scenes.tts: Embed it in a droplet of gel.
scenes.visual: Step card 3 of 4, Embed: the ball sits inside a clear gel droplet, labelled Matrigel.
scenes.narration: Embed it in a droplet of gel.

scenes.tts: Then spin it in a flask, where moving medium brings more oxygen and nutrients.
scenes.visual: Step card 4 of 4, Spin: droplets swirl in a spinning bioreactor; small arrows of medium flow past them.
scenes.narration: Then spin it in a flask, where moving medium brings more oxygen and nutrients.

scenes.tts: Nothing tells these cells where they are in a body. Which features appear on their own?
scenes.visual: Question card listing four options: progenitor zones around a cavity; outer-radial-glia-like cells; the six layers of mature cortex; blood vessels.
scenes.narration: Nothing tells these cells where they are in a body. Which features appear on their own?

scenes.tts: Zones of progenitors form around a fluid-filled cavity. Young neurons settle outside them.
scenes.visual: Time-lapse cross-section of the organoid: a cavity opens, a teal ring of progenitors forms around it, and lighter neurons gather outside. Ticks appear beside the first two options.
scenes.narration: Zones of progenitors form around a fluid-filled cavity. Young neurons settle outside them.

scenes.tts: No one placed these cells. They arranged themselves. That is self-organization, the idea behind every organoid.
scenes.visual: The cross-section completes on its own; a label fades in: self-organization.
scenes.narration: No one placed these cells. They arranged themselves. That is self-organization, the idea behind every organoid.

scenes.tts: But the six layers of mature cortex form at best partly. And a standard organoid has no blood vessels.
scenes.visual: Crosses appear beside the last two options: six layers, at best partial; blood vessels, none.
scenes.narration: But the six layers of mature cortex form at best partly. And a standard organoid has no blood vessels.

scenes.tts: Now set a fetal cortex beside it. Some of what builds it comes from the cells, some from the body around them.
scenes.visual: Split screen: the organoid section on the left, a fetal cortex section on the right with matching teal zones. Amber elements surround the fetal side.
scenes.narration: Now set a fetal cortex beside it. Some of what builds it comes from the cells, some from the body around them.

scenes.tts: Blood vessels bring oxygen. Microglia, the brain's immune cells, arrive from outside. Axons bring input from the thalamus.
scenes.visual: On the fetal side, amber elements are labelled one by one: blood vessels, microglia arriving from outside, thalamic axons.
scenes.narration: Blood vessels bring oxygen. Microglia, the brain's immune cells, arrive from outside. Axons bring input from the thalamus.

scenes.tts: And interneurons stream in from another region, the ventral forebrain.
scenes.visual: A stream of amber interneurons enters the fetal cortex from below, labelled from the ventral forebrain.
scenes.narration: And interneurons stream in from another region, the ventral forebrain.

scenes.tts: In a single organoid, most of these are missing.
scenes.visual: The same amber elements fade out on the organoid side; the teal zones remain.
scenes.narration: In a single organoid, most of these are missing.

scenes.tts: Here is the one idea to carry through. The cells bring the program. The embryo brings the surroundings.
scenes.visual: Rule card: The cells bring the program (teal); the embryo brings the surroundings (amber).
scenes.narration: Here is the one idea to carry through. The cells bring the program. The embryo brings the surroundings.

scenes.tts: An organoid keeps the program and loses most of the surroundings.
scenes.visual: The card adds: an organoid keeps the program and loses most of the surroundings.
scenes.narration: An organoid keeps the program and loses most of the surroundings.

scenes.tts: So trust it most for what the cells do on their own. Test it hardest wherever development needs something from outside. And measure every feature, because the dish adds stress of its own.
scenes.visual: Closing card, labelled a first guess: trust it most for what the cells do on their own; test it hardest where development needs something from outside; measure every feature.
scenes.narration: So trust it most for what the cells do on their own. Test it hardest wherever development needs something from outside. And measure every feature, because the dish adds stress of its own.
